33.0.0.en: Although the people of God fell into the worship of idols and departed from God, He did not reject them but remained faithful to His promises despite their unfaithfulness. So He spoke to Moses that he might prepare to enter the Promised Land, as God had promised the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

33.0.1.en: Be steadfast in your love for those around you, even if they wrong you or do not respond to your love... Make excuses for them, and know that the continuance of your love and care for them establishes you in love and gradually affects them, and qualifies you to receive many divine blessings, the first of which is that you enjoy a strong experience of the love of God and His work in your life.

33.1.0.en: God promised to bring them into the Promised Land, but their leader would be an angel whom God would send, and not God Himself, because of His anger against them on account of their worship of idols.

33.2.0.en: Flowing with milk and honey: an expression for the many good things they will find in the Promised Land. The reason God would not lead them Himself on their way to the Promised Land, which is full of good things, is that they are quick to disobey and rebel, so they deserve the wrath of God and are exposed to destruction, that is, God would destroy them as a punishment for them.

33.3.0.en: The people felt their sin when they heard from Moses that God refused to lead them, and they wept in repentance before God, declaring their sin and asking forgiveness from Him. They stripped off their ornaments as a declaration of their clinging to God and their rejection of anything material for His sake.

33.4.0.en: Horeb: the place where they made the golden calf.

33.4.1.en: God affirmed the obstinacy of the people, signified by the stiffness of the neck, as animals are stubborn and turn and twist their necks, refusing to bear the yoke, that is, the wood that is placed on their necks to pull the agricultural implements. Therefore God withdrew from leading them Himself, yet in His tenderness He gave them an opportunity to repent by saying, "put off your ornaments," that is, repent and humble yourselves before Me, and I will consider what to do with you. So they hastened to repentance, humility and prayer, and put off their ornaments. Putting off ornaments was a well-known practice used in the East as a sign of mourning.

33.4.2.en: (2) God speaks in the tabernacle (v. 7: 11:) 7 And Moses took the tabernacle, and pitched it without the camp, afar off from the camp, and called it the Tabernacle of the congregation. And it came to pass, that every one which sought the LORD went out unto the tabernacle of the congregation, which was without the camp. 8 And it came to pass, when Moses went out unto the tabernacle, that all the people rose up, and stood every man at his tent door, and looked after Moses, until he was gone into the tabernacle. 9 And it came to pass, as Moses entered into the tabernacle, the cloudy pillar descended, and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and the LORD talked with Moses. 10 And all the people saw the cloudy pillar stand at the tabernacle door: and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man in his tent door. 11 And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle.

33.5.0.en: Moses had a tent in which he met with the elders of Israel and judged the people, and this was different from the tent in which he lived with his family. He moved this tent outside the camp, that is, the place where the children of Israel pitched their tents, as a declaration of God's wrath, which was still upon His people, until they completed their repentance. Everyone of the people who had a request before God would go out to this tent and ask Moses to pray for him and would seek God in this place. This shows the mercy of God, who did not forsake them completely but only showed His displeasure with them so that they would repent.

33.5.1.en: This tent is a symbol of the Church, because in it God meets with His people, so it was called the tabernacle of meeting. It is a prelude to the tabernacle of meeting and of the testimony, in which is the Ark of the Covenant, the pattern of which Moses saw on the mountain because it had not yet been made (chs. 25-27).

33.5.2.en: Every need you feel, present it to God in the Church, place it on the altar. For when God sees your faith and your clinging to Him and your hastening to Him, and not to reason, the world and people, He has compassion on you, solves all your problems and blesses your life.

33.6.0.en: When Moses went out from his tent, in which he lived with his family, and passed through the tents of Israel on his way to the tabernacle of meeting outside the camp, everyone would come out of his tent and stand in respect for him and ask for prayer for himself and his family, and they would remain standing in reverence until he reached the tabernacle of meeting and entered it to meet with God.

33.7.0.en: God would declare His presence and His being with Moses, when he entered the tabernacle of meeting, by the pillar of cloud descending, covering, and standing before the door of the tabernacle until God's talk with Moses was finished. Moses would hear Him clearly and speak with Him, and then report to the people God's commands and commandments. Therefore he was called the one to whom God spoke, because of the abundance of His speaking with him. Because of his righteousness he reached the degree of direct conversation with God. By this he was able to lead the people with God's guidance, so that every servant and every head of a family may learn that prayer is the foundation of his success in leading those he serves and cares for.

33.8.0.en: When the people saw God appearing in the pillar of cloud, they would fear and bow down at once, each one before the door of his tent, in reverence and humility, asking for the mercies of God.

33.9.0.en: A wonderful friendship of the highest level was enjoyed by Moses with God through his successive meetings with Him in the tabernacle. His servant and disciple Joshua the son of Nun accompanied him and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and when Moses finished speaking with God and went to the people to teach them, Joshua would remain in the tabernacle in continual prayers and worship. Thus we see how God prepared Joshua through his discipleship to Moses and his learning worship for long periods, as he left his family and stayed in the tabernacle until the tabernacle of the testimony was made, in which is the Ark, and the Levites became responsible for guarding it and being present in it. Notice that this temporary tent was outside the camp as a declaration of God's wrath, but after they offered repentance, Moses set up the permanent tabernacle of meeting in the midst of the camp.

33.10.s.en: (3) Moses' intercession that God might lead His people

33.10.0.en: Moses appealed to God and said to Him, You commanded me to bring up this people and take them to the land of Canaan, and You did not tell me whom You will send with me, meaning that You refused to lead the people Yourself, as You Yourself brought us out of the land of Egypt into the wilderness. He pleaded with Him to lead them and bear with them and not send with them only an angel, and he based his appeal on the following:

33.10.1.en: (1) God said, You have declared that You know me by name, that is, that You have loved me.

33.10.2.en: (2) In humility Moses declared his ignorance in leading the people and his need of God to make the way known to him. (3) Moses showed his longing to know God, as though he did not yet know Him, although he had a long fellowship with Him; he is ambitious to know God every day more than before.

33.10.3.en: (4) He reminds God that the children of Israel are His own people, for whom He is responsible, for He is their Father, their Shepherd and their God.

33.10.4.en: God is very tender, so ask of Him all that you want, and whatever your sins may be, know that He is ready to forgive you, and even if He is angry with you, continue in your supplication and humility before Him until you obtain His mercies.

33.11.0.en: God agreed, before the appeal of Moses, to go Himself in the midst of His people and lead them. Moses affirmed that he would not move with this people except under the leadership of God, for remaining in the wilderness with God is better than entering the Promised Land with all its good things without God, because he loved God above all the material things of the world and found in Him his rest and reassurance.

33.12.0.en: Moses continues his talk with God, declaring that the reason for his distinction and that of his people from all the peoples of the earth is the presence of God in their midst. He is the most precious thing in his life and the life of his people, and by this this people declare their faith in God to the whole world, so that they may believe and join the people of God and find their salvation. In the face of Moses' love and clinging to God, God affirmed to him that He would go before him and would not leave them, because He loved Moses and found in him righteousness and holiness.

33.13.0.en: Moses made a wonderful request that no one had made before, namely to see God. Although he had spoken with Him much, his longing for God led him to make this request.

33.14.0.en: I will make all My goodness pass before you: I will present My mercies before you, and My blessings and My good things.

33.14.1.en: I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you: I will declare Myself before you so that you may believe in Me and live with Me, you and your people. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy: I give My love to whom I choose, and he is the one who believes in Me and responds to Me, and I pour out mercies upon him.

33.14.2.en: God said to him, I will give you many blessings and declare My name before you and have mercy on you, so you will see Me through these blessings and declarations and mercies, and this is quite enough.

33.15.0.en: God said to Moses, I love you and you have found grace in My sight, but this request of yours is beyond your endurance, for no man can see Me, meaning the seeing of the essence of God, because he would die from the greatness of the light of God and His brightness, which exceeds the capacities of human beings. For the angels, who are great creatures, cannot look at God but hide their faces from the brightness of His glory (Isa 6:2).

33.16.0.en: The tenderness of God could not bear, before the request of Moses and his insistence, to deprive His son of seeing Him, so He let him see Him to the extent that he could bear. God took Moses upon a rock and put him in a cleft and covered him with His hand, and then God passed by in His glory, that is, a great dazzling light appeared. Then God lifted His hand, and Moses saw something of the brightness of God, which is what he could bear as a man. He rejoiced greatly, and indeed his face was clothed with intense radiance, so that the children of Israel afterward could not bear to look at him and asked him to put a veil over his face (ch. 34:34, 35). Moses' seeing of God signifies the Incarnation of Christ. When God said, "Behold, there is a place by me," He meant the fullness of time when Christ became incarnate in Bethlehem, and the rock signifies Christ, upon whom the believer stands and sees God, and He reveals to him as much as he can bear. This is what we behold in the New Testament at Communion from the Holy Mysteries, and as God reveals Himself to His saints in the wildernesses throughout the ages. All this we behold now on earth, but in heaven we shall be able to see Him more clearly. Here we see Him as in a mirror, but there face to face, where our earthly bodies are changed and become spiritual bodies able to enjoy the sight of God clearly (1 Cor 13:10-12).

33.16.1.en: God loves you and wants to reveal His secrets to you if you want Him and seek Him. This appears in your striving toward prayer, reading and meditation, for in proportion to your care God will let you experience Him and rejoice in Him. The renewal of the covenant

34.0.0.en: God asked Moses to cut two tablets so that God might write on them the Ten Commandments. So he cut the two tablets in a reasonable size that could be carried and also afterward placed in the Ark of the Covenant. Notice that the two tablets the first time were made by the hand of God, but the second time Moses made them, so that God might show them the result of their sin in worshiping the golden calf, which angered Moses so that he broke the tablets.

34.0.1.en: Do not be careless in seizing every spiritual opportunity to draw near to God and to thank Him for His gifts, lest these blessings be lost to you and you not find them even if you seek them much.

34.1.0.en: He commanded him to rise early in the morning and go up with the tablets on the mountain to its top, that is, its head, which is most likely the same place where God appeared to him the first time and gave him the commandments.

34.2.0.en: He also commanded him that no man go up with him, as the first time, such as Aaron and Joshua, because God would appear to him more and give him more blessings, such as the radiance of his face. He also commanded that no one come near the mountain, not even the animals, so that all might feel its awe and holiness. Moses carried out the word of God and went up with the tablets on the mountain.

34.3.0.en: He stood with him there: Moses stood in the cleft in which God had put him (ch. 33:22). After Moses went up to the top of the mountain, God appeared to him in the form of a great cloud, and then he heard a voice from heaven proclaiming that God had come. This stirs feelings of awe and fear and at the same time longing and love within Moses.

34.4.0.en: God moved before him in the form of a great cloud, which may have been accompanied by a strong light, and then he heard a voice calling the name of the LORD, and the repetition of this was a confirmation of the presence of God Himself, and declaring the attributes of God, which are: (1) Mercy and tenderness toward His people, and pity and compassion for them.

34.4.1.en: (2) Longsuffering, for He does not become angry with His people quickly if they err and gives them an opportunity to repent. (3) His gifts are many and never end.

34.5.0.en: He will by no means clear the guilty: He will not forgive those who persist in sin, whether fathers or children. The voice continues the attributes of God, saying:

34.5.1.en: (5) God gives His blessings to His people however large their number, whether in the same generation or in the following generations.

34.5.2.en: (6) God is forgiving to all who repent, whatever their sins.

34.5.3.en: (7) God is just, so He does not forgive the one who does not repent and persists in sin, and He punishes the children and grandchildren if they walk in the sins of their fathers.

34.5.4.en: Enjoy the mercies of God, for He is tender beyond all imagination, and seize every opportunity for repentance, and do not be lax with any sin however small, and do not justify it, because He is also just.

34.6.0.en: If now I have found grace in Your sight: since I have found grace in Your sight.

34.6.1.en: Moses felt the fear of God and the greatness of His love, so he showed his submission to Him by bowing down on behalf of himself and all his people, and asked of God:

34.6.2.en: (1) That He go in the midst of His people and bear with their obstinacy and disobedience and give them an opportunity to repent. (2) That He forgive the sins of his people because they felt their sin.

34.6.3.en: (3) That He have compassion on His people and accept to be King over them.

34.7.0.en: When God found Moses' response, He promised him not only forgiveness and mercy but the doing of great and awesome wonders, such as their crossing the Jordan River and victory over the peoples dwelling in the land of Canaan. Thus God renewed His covenant with His people.

34.8.0.en: God declared His covenant with His people with His many blessings mentioned in His previous attributes, and as for the people, their undertaking appears in the following:

34.8.1.en: (1) Not making a treaty with the wicked inhabitants of the land in Canaan, lest the children of God mingle with them and be defiled by their evil. This happened, sadly, in the days of the Judges.

34.9.0.en: Their pillars (sacred stones): stone pillars set up for the pagan gods.

34.9.1.en: Their wooden images (Asherim): wooden poles set up on the high places for the gods of the sky, such as the stars.

34.9.2.en: (2) Tearing down the altars and the pillars and cutting down the wooden images, as a rejection of pagan worship, because the children of Israel worship God, and He is jealous over them like a bridegroom over his bride, and He is very angry if they mix His worship with their worship of idols.

34.10.0.en: (3) Not making a treaty with the wicked, lest they mingle with them and flatter them and so take part in the worship of their idols and eat what is sacrificed to them, and by this commit spiritual adultery by leaving the worship of God and turning to the worship of idols.

34.11.0.en: (4) Not letting their sons marry pagan women, lest they draw them into the worship of idols and so they fall into spiritual adultery.

34.12.0.en: (5) He warned them against imitating the pagans in making images and worshiping them.

34.13.0.en: (6) He stressed to him some positive laws that He had mentioned to him the previous time when He gave him the two tablets, so He reminded him to keep the feast of the Passover and the days of Unleavened Bread that follow it, seven days, that is, the feast of Unleavened Bread at the beginning of the seven days and at their end, as was mentioned before (ch. 12), in sanctification of their coming out of the land of Egypt in the month of Abib.

34.14.0.en: (7) He also reminded him of the law of redemption, because God killed the firstborn of Egypt and redeemed the firstborn of His people. So every firstborn is offered to God, and likewise the firstborn of the animals, except the donkey, which is redeemed with a lamb (ch. 13). Thus he does not appear before God empty-handed but offers his gifts to God. This was explained before in (ch. 23).

34.15.0.en: (8) He reminded him to keep the law of the Sabbath, which is the fourth commandment, even if it be in the season of plowing or harvest (ch. 20:4).

34.16.0.en: (9) He also alerted him to the feasts of Weeks and Ingathering (ch. 23).

34.17.0.en: (10) He commanded him to keep the three feasts, that is, the Passover, Weeks (Pentecost) and Ingathering (Tabernacles), at which all the males come to celebrate before God. He promised him, if he keeps the commandments of God, the following: (a) The driving out of the pagans, the inhabitants of the land.

34.17.1.en: (b) He will bless his land and grant him to possess the Promised Land. The borders of the kingdom of the children of Israel were greatly enlarged in the days of Solomon (1 Kgs 4:21), but they shrank when they fell into many sins, and indeed the enemies occupied it completely during the captivity.

34.17.2.en: (c) None of the pagans will covet or dare to enter his land when his males go up to celebrate the three feasts of God.

34.18.0.en: (11) He warns him against using leaven at the feast of the Passover or leaving any of its meat until the next day, as was mentioned before in (ch. 12).

34.19.0.en: (12) He commanded him to bring the firstfruits of his produce to God (ch. 23). (13) He commanded him not to boil a young kid that is still nursing (ch. 23).

34.19.1.en: If you want to enjoy the mercies of God, you must keep His commandments with all care, and if you err, repent quickly, and then He fulfills all His covenants to you.

34.20.0.en: God asked Moses to write the laws that He had told him in a book, so that he might teach them to the people and they might not forget them, and might be committed to them, and so keep the covenant of God and receive His blessings.

34.21.0.en: Moses spent forty days and forty nights with God fasting; he neither ate nor drank during them, and this was by divine help and power. This is the second time of Moses' fasting forty days and forty nights; the first was when he received the two tablets the first time (ch. 24:18), and Elijah fasted the like (1 Kgs 19:18), and then Christ (Mt 4:2). This fast is a miracle that exceeds the capacities of human beings and was accomplished by the power of God. Moses spent this period praying for Aaron and all the people, and God may have stressed to him some commandments and laws that were mentioned before (chs. 21-24), and the design of the tabernacle and its erection (chs. 25-31), and at its end God commanded him to write the Ten Commandments on the two tablets that Moses had made. Notice here that the two tablets the second time were made by Moses and not by God, as a discipline for him because he became angry and in the heat of his anger broke the first two tablets, which God Himself had made. Then God wrote the Ten Commandments on the two tablets with His finger.

34.21.1.en: Do not fear the difficulty of the commandment or of the spiritual practices of prayers and fasts, because God will give you help to fulfill them and to enjoy in them fellowship with God.

34.22.0.en: After Moses received the two tablets of the law the second time from God, He gave him a grace, which was that his face shone with a great radiance as a declaration of his righteousness and holiness, so that the people would submit to him and obey the words of God on his tongue. So God adorns His children in every generation with virtues that they do not see, because of their humility, but people notice in them very clearly.

34.22.1.en: God is ready to give you a special grace so that others may revere and respect you, and you may show them the word of God. Therefore be careful in your speech and remember that you are the voice of God to those around you, so let no evil word come out of your mouth.

34.23.0.en: Moses came down from the mountain and went to meet the people under the leadership of Aaron, and they were this time waiting for him with care, and were surprised by the radiance of his face and feared greatly and felt the fear of God when he approached them, which made them keep further and further from their sins.

34.24.0.en: Moses approached Aaron and the leaders of the people, who were in great fear of the radiance of his face, and he spoke to them all that God had commanded him. Then he approached the people, who also feared the brightness of his face, and perhaps they looked at the ground in humility because they could not bear to see the radiance of his face, and he also told them of the commands of God.

34.25.0.en: Moses did not know that his face was shining, but the people told him of it, and indeed declared that they could not bear to see the radiance of his face and asked him to cover it. So out of pity for them he put a veil or covering on his face when he approached them and taught them. And when he left them and entered the tabernacle of meeting to speak with God, he would remove the veil from his face.

34.25.1.en: There is another opinion in the interpretation of this part, that Moses, besides removing the veil in his talk with God in the tabernacle, would keep the veil removed when teaching the people so that they might feel the fear of God, and then put it back on his face in his ordinary talk with the people.

34.25.2.en: St. Paul the Apostle spoke of this veil in (2 Cor 3:7-18) to show that the knowledge of God was still obscure in the Law, but in the New Testament it appeared clearly.

34.25.3.en: The veil signifies your weakness and your inability to see the works of God and His glory. The more you live a life of repentance, the more you can hear the voice of God and see His works in all the events around you, and you can understand His word in the Holy Bible. Ask for His help in humility, and He will remove from you every barrier that hinders you from sensing Him and understanding Him.

34.25.4.en: The preparation for the tabernacle of meeting
